thread:
marie: Hey — trying to import a customer model from a private HF repo with `redwood-convert` and running into two things: 1) download/auth failing intermittently (401) and 2) safetensors shard missing error. Also saw a runtime complaint about an unexpected weight key `lm_head_merged`. Anyone seen this combo?

ajay: paste the exact errors? 401 usually means token/scope or revision pinning. missing shard could be index mismatch.

marie: here are the logs (trimmed):

```
INFO: huggingface_hub.hf_hub_download repo_id=org/model revision=release-2026-02-05
HTTPError: 401 Client Error: Unauthorized for url: https://huggingface.co/api/models/org/model/resolve/release-2026-02-05/pytorch_model-00001-of-00008.safetensors
...
ERROR: safetensors.common: Missing shards for metadata: expected 00001..00008 but only found 00000,00002,00003,00004,00005,00006,00007,00008
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "convert.py", line 312, in main
    load_state_dict(...)
RuntimeError: Unexpected weight key in checkpoint: lm_head_merged
```

marie: note the repo is private and we passed `--hf-token` to the convert tool.

kevin: couple of thoughts:
- 401 + intermittent = token expiry or wrong scope. hf tokens need `read` scope for private models. are you rotating tokens or using a short-lived infra token?
- missing shard list looks like the converter requested `pytorch_model-00001-of-00008.safetensors` but the repo index includes a slightly different shard naming (we've seen off-by-one when an `.index.json` was generated after a forced re-upload).
- `lm_head_merged` sounds like a weight-key rename that some training pipelines do when merging heads. converter should tolerate unknown keys or map them.

gabi: fwiw we saw something similar last quarter: huggingface_hub will return 200 for the `index.json` but 401 for the actual shard URLs if the token was only authorized for the dataset-level API vs direct file resolves. Try hitting the resolve URL directly with the same token: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $HF_TOKEN" https://huggingface.co/org/model/resolve/release-2026-02-05/pytorch_model.safetensors.index.json` and compare the list to the repo files in the web UI.

marie: did that, here's the index.json snippet: `{\"metadata\":{},\"weight_map\":{\"pytorch_model-00001-of-00008.safetensors\": [\"model.transformer.wte_0\"],\"pytorch_model-00002-of-00008.safetensors\": [...]}}` but when I list the repo files the web UI shows `pytorch_model-00000-of-00008.safetensors` instead of `00001` for the first one.

ajay: aha — sounds like an index vs storage mismatch. Possibly the model was re-generated and the index wasn't re-uploaded or the converter is not using the index mapping but inferring shard names by numeric range. Converter should always prefer `.index.json` when present.

convert-bot: Conversion run 1776001234 failed with exit code 1 (Missing shards). Issue template: please attach model repo and revision.

kevin: short-term hack: manually download all shards via the web UI (or `hf_hub_download` with explicit filenames from the index) and run the converter locally with `--local-checkpoint /path/to/downloads`. Longer-term fix: add a check that compares requested shard list vs `.index.json` and errors with a clear message before attempting downloads. Also add tolerant key mapping for common renames (`lm_head` <-> `lm_head_merged`).

marie: workaround worked — downloaded shards manually and convert finished, but we had to patch config.json to change `tie_word_embeddings` -> `tie_weights` (the customer's training infra writes the old key). After patch convert ran.

gabi: for the auth side, double-check token scope and if you're using a CI-provided token, ensure it has `read` and is not an ephemeral SSO token. There's also an HF header quirk when using `X-Authorization` vs `Authorization` in some older clients.

ajay: action items:
- marie: open a reproducible issue with a minimal private-repo repro (index.json + renamed keys + example revision) and link the logs.
- kevin: add index.json preferred-path check and improve error message + add mapping for common weight-key renames.
- gabi: add a small doc blurb on required HF token scopes and curl examples.

marie: filing issue now and attaching the index + config.json. thanks all — saved me a lot of time. :thumbsup:

kevin: I can PR the converter check tomorrow, will ping you for the repro.

marie: great — I'll drop the repro link here when it's up.

convert-bot: Issue created: redwood-convert#472 (link withheld)

marie: posted the repro: https://hf.co/internal-repro/org/model-repro (private) — @kevin please try with that revision, it reproduces the shard/index mismatch and the `lm_head_merged` key.

ajay: noted. I'll add an e2e test that downloads a model with `.index.json` present and asserts the converter uses the index mapping rather than numeric inference.

marie: thanks everyone — will follow up on the PR and doc updates.
